hello.text: The Archive Halls are hushed: shelves of data crystal under amber light, and the soft tick of a reading desk older than most colonies. A woman at the nearest desk doesn't look up. "If you're lost, the commons is one deck down. If you're selling something, it's two."

choices.text: "Mara sent me. She said you pay captains to recover lost records."
"Ines Okafor at the Deep Space Network sent me."
"I have a recording nobody can decode."

browse.text: "Then look quietly." She turns a page. Then her eyes slide to the slate at her elbow, which shows the docking log, and stop. She looks at you properly for the first time. "That's not a ship I know. And I know all of them."

onekind.text: "Nothing is one of a kind, Captain. Things are just the first of their kind that someone wrote down." She goes back to her page, but she doesn't turn it. "Come back if you have something worth reading."

choices.text: "Actually, I do. The New Horizons transmission."

mara.text: A flicker of a smile, there and gone. "Mara sends me the interesting ones and keeps the charming ones for herself." She closes her book. "Which are you?"

choices.text: "Interesting. I have a clean copy of the New Horizons transmission."

both.text: "Statistically, no." But she almost laughs, which you suspect is rare. "What have you brought me?"

choices.text: "A clean copy of the New Horizons transmission."

okafor.text: "Ines." Something in her face softens and then locks again. "She wouldn't send anyone to me unless the Deep Space Network was out of its depth." She clears a space on the desk. "Show me."

recording.text:
She plugs your recording into a desk older than both of you. The message crawls past, WOLF 359, BARNARD'S STAR, ALPHA CENTAURI, SOL, and she doesn't flinch. Then she strips the words away and leaves only what's underneath: a low carrier tone, rising and falling like a held breath.

Ilse stops breathing too.

"I've heard this before," she says quietly. "Once. Twelve years ago."

choices.text: "There's another signal. From the Oort. Every night at the same hour."
"I heard something like it once. At a colony where everyone vanished."
"You've gone pale. Are you all right?"

oort.text:
Her hand stops over the console. "The Oort," she repeats, carefully, as if the word might break. "Tell me the hour." You tell her. She writes it down on paper, not on the slate, and slips the paper into her coat.

"Interesting," is all she says. It is very clearly not all she thinks.

choices.text: "Where did you hear the tone before?"

silent.text: "Then you know what a quiet world looks like." She studies you for longer than is polite. "Most people who tell me that are lying or drunk. You're neither."

choices.text: "Where did you hear the tone before?"

pale.text: "I'm an archivist. We're all pale." A beat. "But thank you for asking. Nobody does."

ninefold.text:
"The Ninefold. A survey tender owned by a research consortium at Lalande 21185." She pulls up a record: a squat, ugly little ship. "Its last transmission had this same tone under it, and then nothing. The consortium went bankrupt a year later, and the Archive bought their records at auction."

Her eyes flick to the window, to your ship in the dock.

"The same auction your ship came from, I'd guess."

choices.text: "You knew what my ship was the moment I docked."

knew.text:
"I knew she was consortium-built. The hull lines give it away." A pause; a decision. "And I knew her drive core wasn't on any parts list we bought. I've been waiting twelve years for someone to fly her in here."

It's more honest than she meant to be. You watch her regret it.

choices.text: "Then tell me where the Ninefold is."

where.text: "Drifting at Wolf 359. A miner reported the wreck years ago and nobody cared." She slides a data chit across the desk. "Her flight recorder should still be aboard. Bring it back and the Archive pays well." She stands and takes her coat off the chair. "One condition. A record never leaves an archivist's sight. I'm coming with you."

choices.text: "Why do you really want to come?"

rules.text: "Naturally, Captain. I'll follow every rule you can explain to me." She says it so politely that it takes you a moment to notice it was a threat.

why.text: "Because it's the most interesting thing that's happened to me in twelve years, and I refuse to read about it secondhand." True, but not the whole truth. You can tell, and she can tell that you can tell.

choices.text: "I'll get the rest of it out of you eventually."

pack.text: She packs in under a minute: a slate, a coat, and three paper books held together with a strap. "Wolf 359, then." She pauses at the hatch of your ship and lays her palm flat on the hull, like someone greeting a horse. "Hello," she tells it, very quietly.

look.text:
A consortium survey tender, NINEFOLD stenciled on her flank, tumbling slowly in Wolf 359's red light. Every hatch is welded shut, and from the scorch pattern, the welding was done from the inside.

Without the consortium's access codes you'd be cutting for hours, and something about her makes you not want to stay that long.

choices.text: Mark her on the chart and move on.

a.text: You match the Ninefold's slow tumble and dock. Every hatch is welded shut. From the inside.

choices.text: "Ilse, do the Archive's codes still open consortium locks?"

codes.text: "They should." On the suit channel you hear her typing, then a heavy clunk deep in the hull. "There. She remembers who owns her."

cut.text: Twenty minutes with the torch. The weld gives with a crack, and a breath of old air puffs out past you and freezes into glitter.

in.text: Frost on everything. Your helmet light is the only light. Somewhere deeper in the ship, something metal ticks as it cools, or warms. It's hard to tell which.

a.text: The table is set for six. Six coffee cups, still full, frozen solid. Someone left a card game in the middle of a hand: four of them face down, two face up, one chair pushed back as if its owner had just stood to answer something.

ilse.text: "I see it." Her light lingers on the empty chair. "Everyone else stayed sitting." A pause. "Whatever called, it called one of them first."

a.text:
Six bunks. The lockers stand open and empty, as if everyone packed in a hurry. On one bunk a photo is still taped to the frame: six people in survey jackets, squinting into a sunlit dock, one of them holding up a hand-lettered sign that reads NINEFOLD OR BUST.

The bunk underneath it has the name OKONKWO stenciled on the frame. Someone has scratched lines into the metal beside the name. Not a tally. A wave: rising, falling, rising.

choices.text: Trace the scratches with your light.

wave.text: You've seen this shape before. On Okafor's screen, on Ilse's desk: the carrier tone under the core signal. Scratched in by hand, over and over, deeper each time, until the last one goes right through the frame.

a.text:
Ration crates, mostly empty. Survey drones in their foam, never launched. And wedged behind the last crate, a tube of paper charts, the old-fashioned kind survey crews carry in case everything else fails.

You unroll the top one. The outer Oort Cloud, hand-plotted. One point far out past Pluto is circled three times, with a note in shaky capitals: FOUND IT HERE.
Empty ration crates and a few survey drones nobody will ever launch. You already have the charts.

The cargo bay is huge and empty except for one thing: a cradle bolted to the deck, shaped to hold something roughly the size of your own ship's drive core. Its bolts have been sheared, not unscrewed.

Someone has scrawled on it in marker: SOLD - TALLIS CAMP - CINDER. And under that, smaller, in a different hand: it hums.

Beside the cradle, neatly side by side, is a pair of boots. Just the boots.

bridge.text: The bridge consoles are dead and furred with frost. The flight recorder sits in its armored housing behind the pilot's seat. You pull it free. When its power cell touches your suit, it plays its last log on its own.

log.text:
"Log, day 311. We pulled something out of the Oort. Big, warm, old. It hums when the signal plays. The consortium is paying a fortune for it."

"Day 340. Payroll's late again. Sold the scrap off the outer hull to the miners on Cinder. They didn't ask what it was."

"Day 352. It's singing back. Okonkwo says it's only resonance. Okonkwo has been lying in the cargo bay for two days with his ear pressed to the cradle, and he won't come out."

Then static, and under the static, a sound like breathing.

ilse.text:
Ilse's voice on the suit channel is very calm, which is how you know she's frightened. "Big, warm, old." She takes a breath. "Captain, the consortium only built one ship after this. Yours."

She doesn't have to finish.

choices.text: "I know. Let's get out of here."

take.text: The recorder goes into your pack. It's heavier than it should be.

a.text: The empty recorder housing. Frost has already started to grow back over the place where it sat.

Back aboard, hatch sealed behind you, you notice it for the first time. Your drive core, the part of her that's older than the rest, is humming. Very softly. In time with the recorder in your pack.

A message pings in from the Bessel Archive: fee received, with thanks.

choices.text: Shut the recorder off. Set a course for Cinder.
